tossups.text: In this short story, Clyde Dunbar is unable to attend the central event due to a broken leg.This story sees Old Man Warner say "Next thing you know they'll be wanting to go back to living in caves," after Mr. Adams tells him that some towns are considering giving up the titular event. One character arrives late once she realizes the date is June 27th, and is later told to "Be a good sport" by Mrs. Delacroix after she accuses Mr. Summers of being unfair. That character, Tessie Hutchinson, is the victim of a town ritual. For 10 points, name this Shirley Jackson short story in which townspeople draw slips of paper from a black box to determine a scapegoat.

The protagonist of a novel by this author calls her newborn daughter "a bomb to blow up smugness" at the climax of a speech that she delivers in frustration at the lukewarm response to her proposal for a Community Day. This author wrote that "every compulsion is put upon writers to become safe, polite, obedient, and sterile" in a letter declining the Pulitzer Prize for his novel whose protagonist travels around a Caribbean island, giving away a bacteriophage to cure an outbreak of the plague. This author raised early awareness for the civil rights movement with his novel about a banker based on NAACP leader Walter White, who discovers that he is one-sixty-fourth black. This author of Kingsblood Royal wrote a novel about Carol Kennicott's efforts at reforming the town of Gopher Prairie. For 10 points, name this American author who popularized the term "Main Street" with his novel of that title.

The first chapter of one of this thinker's works addresses the fact that "the family is not the same in all human societies"; that chapter is found in the section "The Formation of a Complex." In addition to attacking the Oedipus complex in Sex and Repression in Savage Society, this thinker wrote a trilogy on the peoples of the Kiriwina Islands in which he discussed the Trobriand islanders' agricultural methods and the Kula ring. For 10 points, name this Polish anthropologist who wrote The Coral Gardens and their Magic and Argonauts of the Western Pacific.

The conservation of this quantity is a consequence of translational invariance according to Noether's theorem. For a particle, the de Broglie wavelength equals the Planck constant divided by this quantity. According to a principle named for Heisenberg, the accurate measurement of position produces uncertainties in the measurement of this quantity. Newton's second law can alternatively be written as force equals the change in this quantity divided by the change in time. Unlike kinetic energy, this quantity is conserved in inelastic collisions. For 10 points, name this vector quantity symbolized by a lowercase p that is equal to an object's mass and velocity.

A god in this religion is cast away in a reed boat after being born deformed because his mother spoke first during a marriage ceremony. A legendary sword in this religion gained its name after being used to escape a burning grassland and was originally found inside the body of an eight-headed serpent. After her brother kills one of her attendants by throwing a flayed horse into her loom, a deity of this religion hides away in a cave. Shrines in this religion such as a "grand" one at Ise ("ee-say") are attended by miko priestesses. A line of emperors traces their lineage back to this religion's sun goddess, Amaterasu. For 10 points, kami are venerated in what indigenous religion of Japan?

This text claims that the word "wait" "rings in the ear" with "piercing familiarity." This text notes that everything Hitler did in Germany was "legal" after its author likens himself to people "willing to face hungry lions." One of the "two honest confessions" in this text decries "a negative peace which is the absence of tension." This text quotes St. Augustine by saying that "an unjust law is no law at all." The author explains his disappointment in the "white moderate" and describes how he is "compelled to carry the gospel of freedom" in this text to his "fellow clergymen." The author of this text wrote "Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere" on a smuggled-in newspaper. For 10 points, name this text by Martin Luther King Jr. written while imprisoned in Alabama.

This king's Earl of Surrey defeated James IV of Scotland at the Battle of Flodden Field, while he personally defeated Louis XII's forces at the Battle of the Spurs. His pamphlet Defense of the Seven Sacraments earned him the title "defender of the faith," though Thomas Cranmer issued the Book of Common Prayer later in his reign. The first Act of Supremacy was passed during the reign of this king after Pope Clement VII refused to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon. For 10 points, name this English king who had six wives.

This god was often depicted with two wolves, Geri and Freki, at his feet. Among this god's possessions is the ring Draupnir [DROWP-"near"], which makes eight copies of itself every nine nights. This god once hung himself on Yggdrasil [IG-druh-sil] for nine days and nine nights to gain knowledge of other worlds and understand the runes. For ten points, name this chief Norse god, the husband of Frigg and the father of Thor.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for colon sections. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this colon-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The colon is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in colon sections.

tossups.text: This man's essay "Search for a Method" introduces his Critique of Dialectical Reason, while one of his titles claims his philosophy is a Humanism. His concepts include "bad faith" and "being-in-itself." This lover of the author of The Second Sex, Simone de Beauvoir, claimed that existence precedes essence in Being and Nothingness. "Hell is other people" is a quote by, for 10 points, what Frenchman whose plays such as No Exit show his existentialism?

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for red blood cells and hemoglobin. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this erythrocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The erythrocyte is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in red blood cells and hemoglobin.

tossups.text: An empirical correlation for the design of apparatus for this process is the Gilliland plot. For small amounts of sample, this process is often performed in a series of horizontally aligned bulbs in the Kugelrohr setup for its "short-path" form. Like chromatography, the efficiency of this process can be considered in terms of a number of theoretical plates. A 95:5 mix of ethanol and water cannot be separated by this technique as it forms an azeotrope. Hydrocarbons of different lengths can be separated from crude oil by the "fractional" type of this process. For 10 points, name this process of separating liquids with different boiling points.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for blood glucose regulation. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this insulin-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The insulin is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in blood glucose regulation.

tossups.text: One ruler from this dynasty ate a locust in the hopes that it would transfer the people's suffering to himself. This dynasty ended a system in which land was doled out based on family size, the equal field system. Yang Guifei was a concubine reluctantly executed by Emperor Xuanzong in this dynasty. This dynasty was founded by Li Yuan, and it was briefly interrupted by the rule of Wu Zetian, China's only female emperor. This dynasty put down the rebellion of An Lushan, and it came between the Sui ["sway"] and Song dynasties. For 10 points, name this dynasty marking the high point of Chinese history, ruling for most of the latter half of the first millennium.

The 11th ruler of this name cried "the city is fallen and I am still alive" before leading a suicidal charge during the fall of his capital. Another ruler of this name fought Maxentius after seeing a cross in the sky, winning the Battle of Milvian Bridge. The first ruler of this name issued the Edict of Milan, recognizing Christianity. For 10 points, give this name of a "Great" Roman Emperor who moved to Byzantium and renamed the city after himself.

A ship named for this man sank the HMS Hood and was hunted by the British Navy. Succeeded by Leo von Caprivi, this man proposed the Three Emperors' League, declared war on Denmark over the province of Schleswig-Holstein, eliminated Catholic influence during the Kulturkampf, and edited a telegram to provoke the Franco-Prussian War. Serving during the rule of Wilhelm I, for 10 points, name this "Iron Chancellor" who led Prussia through the unification of Germany.

In one of this author's stories, a mother prevents her daughter Dee from taking the family quilts from her younger sister Maggie; that work is "Everyday Use." This author wrote about Tashi, who murders the female circumciser M'Lissa, and in another work Brownfeld has an affair at the Dew Drop Inn with his father's lover Josie. In addition to Possessing Secret Joy and The Third Life of Grange Copeland, in another work Corrine and Reverend Samuel take in Nettie, while the protagonist is forced into an abusive marriage with Mr. [blank] before having a relationship with Shug Avery. For 10 points, name this author who wrote about Celie in The Color Purple.

1. A WWII veteran and bigot discovers that his family genealogy can be traced back to a black man named Xavier Pic in one work by this author, and the tyrant Buzz Windrip rules in a dystopian novel by him. In addition to Kingsblood Royal and It Can't Happen Here, this author also wrote two works centering on a hypocritical preacher and a realtor, respectively, both from the town of Zenith. The first American Nobel laureate in Literature, for 10 points, identify this creator of Gopher Prairie and author of Elmer Gantry, Babbitt, and Main Street.

One character in this novel tells a story about why the tortoise's shell is not smooth to her daughter, after which Chielo reveals that the latter must be taken to Agbala, the Oracle. During the Week of Peace, the protagonist breaks the Peace of Ani by beating his youngest wife, and later on, despite the advice of an elder, the protagonist takes part in the murder of Ikemefuna. The protagonist finds that the church in Umuofia has gained strength after he returns from a seven-year exile for the accidental murder of Ezeudu's son, and later leads an unsuccessful revolt against the colonial leaders. As a result, Okonkwo commits suicide at the end of, For 10 points, what novel by Chinua Achebe?

One province in this country recently saw the controversial Nizam-e-adl regulations implemented to assuage local complaints about the slow administration of justice. That province is home to the southern terminus of the Karakoram Highway, as well a more famous transit route running from Jamrud to Torkham, passing through Landi Kotal on the Durand Line. The Swat district and the city of Peshawar are found in that North-West Frontier Province, whose Hasba Bill was opposed by Iftikhar Chaudhry, the head of this country's Supreme Court and major political rival of its President. The PPP continues to challenge the long rule of Pervez Musharraf in, for 10 points, what country with capital at Islamabad? A

parts.text: Name this ancient Roman poet, who stated that traditional Roman virtues had disappeared, such that Rome was no longer Roman.

These 16 poems by Juvenal were sorted into a 5-book collection. This collection shares its name with a genre that ridicules and exposes shortcomings and hypocrisy in institutions, people, and government.
According to the tenth Satire, Romans desire "panem et circenses", which translates to item and "circuses".

bonuses.leadin: The question "Who watches the watchmen?" was posed in the sixth entry of a collection by this man. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this glove factory owner in Old Rimrock and former three-sport athlete. 10 years after running into this high school idol of his at Shea Stadium, the narrator is asked to write a tribute for this man's dead father Lou.
The idyllic life of Seymour "the Swede" Levov is shattered when his daughter Merry bombs a post office in this 1997 novel by Philip Roth.

In an oft-quoted line in literary discussions of the Trump era, Zuckerman says that Merry's actions brought the Swede into the "desperation of the counterpastoral," which he calls the "indigenous American" form of this sentiment.

bonuses.leadin: While meeting this man at an Italian restaurant, the narrator wonders about the "substratum" under this man's perfect facade, only to discover it after this man's death from prostate cancer. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this practice that Malinowski claimed the Trobriand islanders used for open sea fishing, but not lagoon fishing. Malinowski also discussed the Trobrianders' use of this practice for cultivating gardens on coral atolls.

A Malinowski quote about magic closes Horace Miner's essay about "Body Ritual among" this fictional tribe, whose use of a charm-box in a shrine parallels the use of medicine cabinets in American bathrooms.

Stanley Tambiah, an anthropologist from this country, analogized Malinowski's account of the role of magic in the Trobrianders' practical life to Newton and Kepler's interest in the occult. Tambiah also wrote a book about the "Ethnic Fratricide" of this island country's conflict between Sinhalese and Tamils.

bonuses.leadin: George Gmelch argued that Bronislaw Malinowski's description of this practice also applies to American sports in his paper on its "Baseball" type. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these two molecular geometries, which ammonia and water possess, respectively.
This theory, which was developed by Gillespie and Nyholm, and is often known by a five-letter acronym, can be used to predict the geometry of molecules.
Sulfur dioxide, which has a steric number of three and one lone pair, has a shape named for this letter. In the contact process, a pentoxide of the element with this symbol is used as a catalyst.

bonuses.leadin: These two molecular geometries are possessed by molecules with a steric number of four and either one or two lone pairs. For the state number of points:

parts.text: Name this Hindu god of beginnings.

So large were the pasturelands of Atlantis that these large animals thrived. When Shiva decapitated Ganesha his was replaced with a head of one of these animals, which allowed Ganesha to later throw a tusk at the moon.

Ganesha and his six headed brother Skanda were the sons of this woman. In one account, this woman fashioned Ganesha from the dirt on her skin, and she is the reincarnation of Shiva's first consort, Sati.

bonuses.leadin: The moon is forced to wax and wane as a punishment for laughing at this god after his stomach burst from excessive indulgence of candy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this city. A poem asks if "[this city was] builded here, among these dark satanic mills?" and begins with the line "and did those feet in ancient time."

This other poem by the same author describes "when the stars threw down their spears and water'd heaven with their tears" and asks the title animal "what the hammer? what the chain, in what furnace was thy brain?"
"And did those feet in ancient time" and "The Tyger" are by this English poet who wrote Songs of Experience and "London."

bonuses.leadin: In a poem about this city, the narrator commands "Bring me my Spear: O clouds unfold! Bring me my Chariot of fire!" For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this pharaoh who built monuments at Luxor and Karnak, as well as temples at Abydos and Abu Simbel. He won the Battle of Kadesh.
Ramesses built tombs both for his sons and for himself, now known as KV5 and KV7, in this location. Tutankhamen was also buried here.
acceptableAnswers: Valley of the Tombs of the Kings

parts.text: The pyramids of Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure are situated near this city. The Sphinx is also here.

bonuses.leadin: He was the longest-reigning pharaoh, ruling for 66 years, and is noted for building a lot of monuments. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Monkey King, whose incredible memory comes from remembering every monkey on Earth. This character accompanies the monk Tang Sanzang in the Chinese epic Journey to the West.
Sun Wukong tried to steal the peaches to gain this trait. Chinese alchemists added mercury to an elixir to acquire this trait.
acceptableAnswers: any clear reference to living forever

parts.text: Sun Wukong possessed one of these objects, called Ruyi Bang, that could grow or shrink at his command. A sacred snake appears wrapped around one of these objects owned by Asclepius.

bonuses.leadin: This figure becomes trapped under a mountain for 500 years after stealing the Peaches of Heaven. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with adrenal medulla hormones.
What is the main function of the adrenal in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to adrenal medulla hormones.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: This Yoruba-influenced religion initially evolved in Cuba and is popular throughout the Caribbean. It is called Lukumi by its adherents, and is notably not practiced by Sublime.

This religion is an earlier development than Santería, arising when slaves brought to Haiti in the 16th and 17th centuries were forced to convert to the Catholicism of their owners, while still retaining West African religious practices. Its practitioners direct prayers to Loa, lower beings than Bondye, the supreme deity.
This primarily Jamaican religion venerates Haile Selassie and adherents partake of the ganja as spiritual exercise. A particularly notable practitioner was Bob Marley.

bonuses.leadin: Welcome to the Caribbean. Answer some questions about the religions practiced here, for 10 Points Each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with diabetes types.
What is the main function of the insulin in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to diabetes types.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Name this cyclic compound present in uracil and cytosine, which also names a class of nucleobases.

Pyrimidines and purines engage in base pairing using these strongest intermolecular forces. These interactions form between a namesake element on one molecule and a highly electronegative element on another.
Purine nucleobases consist of a pyrimidine ring along with this other ring. This nitrogen heterocycle is present in the side chain of histidine.

bonuses.leadin: A derivative of this compound is treated with bisulfite to synthesize uracil. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with inflammatory response.
What is the main function of the phagocyte in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to inflammatory response.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Name this mineral traded for gold in West Africa because of its food flavoring and preservation abilities.

This empire dominated the Saharan salt trade in the 900s CE thanks to its control of the Taghaza mines. Al-Bakri visited this empire's capital of Koumbi Saleh, which was located in modern-day Mauritania.

Ghana's salt trade was inherited by the Sosso empire, whose king Sumunguru ("soo-muhn-GOO-roo") was defeated by this ruler with a poisoned arrow. An oral epic named for this ruler relates how he became the first Mansa of the Mali empire.

bonuses.leadin: According to Ibn Battuta, the houses of the city of Taoudenni were blocks of this material covered with camel skins. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This man was the president who pardoned Richard Nixon after serving as his vice president.
Another Ford was this man, known for pioneering the use of the assembly line to make cars. His first name is required.
A man named Robert Ford is most famous for assassinating this famous American outlaw and gang leader in 1882.

bonuses.leadin: Answer these questions about notable people with the same last name, for 10 points each:

parts.text: This river has its origins in the Blue and White rivers and, thanks to the Aswan Dam, is not flooding as much as it used to.
This fourth-longest river in Africa is home to the Victoria Falls and enters the Indian Ocean in Mozambique.
This river passes through the cities of Bamako and Timbuktu as well as the capital of its namesake country, Niamey. It enters the Gulf of Guinea.

bonuses.leadin: Name some rivers of Africa, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this poem about a man whose "bellows blow" each work day, written by the author of "The Song of Hiawatha."
This poet of "The Wreck of the Hesperus" wrote "The Village Blacksmith."
This book-length poem by Longfellow follows the title character's search for her love, Gabriel, after their expulsion from Acadia.

bonuses.leadin: The speaker of this poem thanks the title figure for teaching him that "at the flaming forge of life/Our fortunes must be wrought." For 10 points each:

parts.text: African-American poet Phyllis Wheatly addressed this general and future president as "his Excellency", describing how he provoked Britannia to "[droop] the pensive head" during the American Revolution.

This woman celebrated the burning of her house as a gift from God in one poem. She addressed her "Dear and Loving Husband" in another poem that appeared in her book The Tenth Muse Lately Sprung Up in America.
This puritan preacher compared humanity to spiders dangled over a fire in his sermon Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about early American authors, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this position, also held by Robert Pinsky and Rita Dove, which serves as the official consultant on poetry to the United States Congress.
This man, who served as the US Poet Laureate in 1986 and 1987, wrote about the political rise of Willie Stark in the novel All The King's Men.
This other US Poet Laureate wrote that "They begin beating it with a hose to find out what it really means" in his "Introduction to Poetry", and wrote The Art of Drowning.

bonuses.leadin: Charles Simic was the first Serbian-American to hold this post. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this continent, the fifth largest, which is home to research stations such as McMurdo, and Neumayer. It is also the location of the South Pole.
This floating megalith of ice was discovered in 1841 and named after its discoverer. This massive ice shelf on the "southern" coast of Antarctica is approximately the size of France.
This northwestern bay in Antarctica is notable for its cover from heavy winds by Anvers Island and the Argentine cruisers that often show tourists this bay.

bonuses.leadin: This landmass is the driest, windiest continent on Earth, and is home to the world's largest desert. For 10 points each:
